title: catch-up 1: the hub's per-room fanout sequence
description:
docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §4. Assign and persist a monotonic per-room sequence, from 1, one per fanout, covering handshakes as well as application messages, never reused or renumbered. It is not a timestamp, not an MLS epoch, not a message id: accepted_timestamp is milliseconds and is not an ordering key (collisions, and no monotonicity across a clock adjustment).

Carry it BESIDE the message in the POST /notify/{roomId} envelope, not inside FanoutMessage (§4 reading 2, the note's recommendation, subject to Mark settling open question 1). That keeps a structure other implementations already parse unchanged, and the sequence is a property of the delivery rather than of the message.

Store it with the hub's fanout so §3's catch-up can serve by sequence. Fixture tests: a sequence is assigned per fanout in hub order; it survives a restart; it does not restart or skip; two fanouts in the same millisecond get distinct increasing sequences.
design:
Assign and persist a monotonic per-room fanout sequence on the hub.

Starts at 1 for a room's first fanout, increases by one, per room, never
reused or renumbered. It numbers every fanout -- handshake and
application alike -- because a follower that missed a handshake needs it
as much as a message. It is not a timestamp, not an MLS epoch and not a
message id: an epoch covers many application messages.

WIRE PLACEMENT, decided by Mark 2026-11-22 (decision mimid-1wgh.104):
beside the message, in the POST /notify/{roomId} envelope, NOT inside
FanoutMessage. So no other implementation's parser changes, a proxy
cannot strip it without its absence being visible, and the sequence
models the delivery rather than the content.

Still to settle when this is written: whether the envelope carries it as
an HTTP header or as a wrapper object around FanoutMessage. Prefer a
header if franking does not need to cover it; if it must be covered,
a wrapper. Check what the hub signs today in peer.rs before choosing,
and record the choice on this bead.

The sequence must be assigned in the same transaction that records the
fanout, so a crash cannot leave a gap or a duplicate.
notes:
DONE 2026-11-25. The checks this bead asked for are in the note above;
this is what shipped and what it deliberately leaves.

WHAT SHIPPED.

* migrations/0018_fanout_sequence.sql: room.next_fanout_seq (the
  counter), room_event.fanout_seq (so catch-up can serve by it) and
  outbox.fanout_seq (so a delivery after a restart sends the same
  number without matching a body back to an event). A unique index on
  (room_id, fanout_seq) for the non-zero rows, so a duplicate inside a
  room is a constraint failure and not a quiet renumbering. 0 means an
  event or row from before this migration: delivered without a
  sequence, and catch-up cannot name it.
* store/log.rs next_fanout_seq: UPDATE room SET next_fanout_seq =
  next_fanout_seq + 1 ... RETURNING next_fanout_seq - 1, inside the
  transaction insert_event already runs, so a crash leaves neither a
  gap nor a duplicate. Both append_event and append_proposals go
  through it, so handshakes are numbered as well as application
  messages. enqueue_fanout takes one from the same counter, so the two
  paths cannot collide.
* peer.rs FANOUT_SEQUENCE_HEADER = "mimi-fanout-sequence", INVENTED,
  NOT FROM SPEC, named for bead mimid-1wgh.37.104 to propose. Sent by
  notify() only when the sequence is non-zero, through a private
  call_with() so the other ten call sites are untouched.
* provider_auth.rs covers the header when the request carries it. Not
  in SIGNED_COMPONENTS: RFC 9421 §2.5 makes a covered field that is
  absent an error, so every other endpoint would fail to sign.
* docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §4 records the resolution where the open
  question was posed.

TESTS, all five red first.

* store/log.rs a_fanout_sequence_is_per_room_and_starts_at_one -- and
  that every outbox row of one fanout carries that fanout's number.
* store/log.rs a_restart_and_a_prune_do_not_renumber_the_sequence --
  one test for both, because they have the same wrong answer
  (MAX(room_event.fanout_seq)).
* store/log.rs the_clock_does_not_decide_the_sequence -- two fanouts in
  one millisecond, and a clock that goes BACKWARDS.
* tests/hub_fanout.rs each_notify_carries_its_fanout_sequence_beside_the_message
  -- 1, 2, 3 on the wire, with assert_request still requiring the body
  to decode as a NotifyRequest and be byte-identical. That last part is
  the assertion that would have broken had the sequence gone inside
  FanoutMessage, which is what decision mimid-1wgh.104 chose against.
* provider_auth/tests.rs the_fanout_sequence_is_covered_when_it_is_there
  -- a rewritten sequence fails the signature, and a request without
  one does not name the component.

Also fixed: store/mod.rs open_applies_migrations_and_records_domain
pins the exact list of applied migrations, which 0018 was not in. The
test was right to fail.

DELIBERATELY NOT IN SCOPE, and each needs its own bead or the next
catch-up bead:

1. THE FOLLOWER DOES NOT READ THE HEADER. Nothing verifies, stores or
   acts on an arriving sequence, so a gap is still invisible to the
   receiving side. That is the catch-up primitive, §5, and the point of
   the sequence; this bead only assigns and carries it.
2. THE HUB'S OWN-DOMAIN SHORTCUT CARRIES NO SEQUENCE. hub/fanout.rs
   sends a row for its own domain through local.deliver(room_id, body),
   which never touches the wire and so takes no header. The row's
   fanout_seq is assigned and stored either way, so nothing is lost,
   but a local follower learns the sequence from the store rather than
   from a delivery. Worth settling when §5 lands, because catch-up has
   to behave the same for both.
3. NOTHING REFUSES AN EVENT WITH fanout_seq 0 anywhere. Rows from
   before this migration are simply unnameable by catch-up, which §5
   has to handle as a pruned range anyway.
